New Apple CEO John Ternus is planning to "overhaul" Apple in an attempt to make the company "faster and leaner," according to a new report from Bloomberg. The changes include more products, cuts to "middle management," and other shifts.

Here's what John Ternus wants to reshape Apple into

First, the new Apple CEO wants to release more products faster than before, including being "more experimental." One idea is to break up Apple's product release schedule and rely less on traditional spring and fall launch cadences, instead rolling out more new products throughout the year.

Ternus also wants to "build a leaner, more engineering-focused org," which involves several cost-cutting and restructuring measures. One example of a change is "eliminating some middle management positions in order to reduce the layers between engineers and top executives."

The report notes that Apple has fired several Engineering Project Managers (EPMs) in the hardware engineering division over the past two weeks. Bloomberg describes these roles as having "been central to Apple's product development process for decades," responsible for "managing timelines and coordinating work across teams."

"Those affected include multiple project managers, including about six directors, one of the most senior tiers of employees at the company. These employees were given a few weeks to find other positions within Apple; those who don't find new roles will be laid off later this year," the report says.

But cost-cutting measures may expand further, according to Bloomberg. Ternus has reportedly argued for years that Apple should be more "lean":

Also, Apple reportedly canceled a plan this summer to lay off 5,000 AppleCare employees because it believed AI-powered support agents could handle the work.

Meanwhile, Ternus wants to grow Apple's Services revenue alongside Eddy Cue and CFO Kevan Parekh. "They've discussed launching new services, as well as finding more revenue from existing products and services," the report says.
